problems.question: What is the relationship between the first jump shown on the number line and the missing jump needed to reach a total of 15?

options.text: The first jump lands on 13, so you need to jump forward 2 more units to reach 15.
The first jump lands on 13, so you need to jump forward 3 more units to reach 15.
The first jump starts at 7, so you need to jump forward 8 more units to reach 15.
The first jump adds 6, so you need to jump forward 6 more units to reach 15.

problems.rationale: Starting at 7 and adding 6 moves forward 6 units to land at 13. To determine the missing addition step needed to reach 15 from 13, find the difference between 15 and 13, which is 2 units (13 + 2 = 15).
problems.teachingNote: Look for students who choose B by counting the starting point (13, 14, 15 as 3 counts) rather than counting intervals, or C by calculating from the original starting point 7 instead of the intermediate sum 13.
successCriteria: Analyze a multi-step addition model on a number line.
Determine the missing addend required to reach a target sum from an intermediate position.
